title: Autoscale signal debouncing and warmup cohorting: action plan after capacity regression
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a peak traffic window on 2026-03-09 we observed an autoscaling regression that led to sustained cold starts and request latency spikes for ~18 minutes. HPA replica counts trailed demand due to an interaction between percentile-based request-rate smoothing and KEDA trigger suppression logic that treated a correlated multi-tenant burst as noise. Warm pools were not effectively utilized because cohorting logic evicted warm workers prematurely. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, immediate mitigations applied, and the action plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-09 10:05 UTC - Traffic surge begins (client A & B concurrently ramp).
2026-03-09 10:07 UTC - KEDA scaler observed short 95th-percentile spike; autoscaler suppressed scale-up due to configured debounce window.
2026-03-09 10:09 UTC - HPA observed increased queue depth but percentile-smoothing lagged; replica count did not increase.
2026-03-09 10:12 UTC - Warm-pool eviction policy trimmed cohort for the affected pool based on aggregate idle heuristics.
2026-03-09 10:20 UTC - SRE on-call manually triggered emergency scale-up and applied a temporary override policy. Latency began to recover by 10:23 UTC.
2026-03-09 10:25 UTC - Incident declared resolved. Postmortem investigation started the following day.
root_causes: Percentile-based smoothing (configured to 5-minute window and 95th percentile) muted short high-amplitude bursts that should have triggered scale-up.
KEDA trigger debounce/edge-detection treated the burst as measurement noise because multiple clients produced correlated short spikes; scaler did not surface a secondary aggregated metric.
Warm-pool cohort eviction used a global idle threshold that did not account for recent burst histories per cohort, causing premature removal of prewarmed capacity.
Insufficient cross-layer visibility: autoscaler, KEDA metrics, and warm-pool decisions were not correlated in dashboards or alerts, slowing diagnosis.
mitigations_short_term: Lowered KEDA trigger debounce window from 30s to 8s for the affected scaler config (rolled 2026-03-10).
Temporarily increased HPA target percentile sensitivity for request-rate metric (5-min -> 2-min) to reduce smoothing lag during high variance windows.
Disabled aggressive warm-pool eviction for the affected GPU pool for 72 hours to restore headroom for lingering bursts.
Added a runbook step for SRE to inspect correlated client ramps and escalate to on-call platform engineer if aggregated 1m spike exceeds threshold for >2 consecutive minutes.
long_term_plan: Implement an aggregation layer that derives a 'burst-index' combining client-level and global signals so KEDA can use an aggregated burst metric when individual triggers conflict with global demand.
Introduce per-cohort warmup retention buckets (cohorting) that respect recent burst history and provide minimum reserved instances for high-variance workloads.
Replace single-window percentile smoothing with an adaptive smoothing algorithm (multi-window / exponential decay) to be more responsive to short high-amplitude events without amplifying noise.
Add an autoscaler diagnostics endpoint that surfaces raw trigger samples, smoothing windows, and decision rationale for auditability and faster incident TTR.
monitoring_changes: Added a dashboard tile showing 'burst-index' proxy (1m/5m/95p overlay) for every scaler group.
Synthetic alert: fire if HPA desired_replicas < demand_estimate for >60s AND warm_pool_free_capacity < 10%.
SLO instrumentation: capture 'scale-decision-latency' metric (time between sustained demand crossing scale threshold and HPA scaling action).
Log enrichment: include scaler decision reason in platform request tracing span for any request that experiences cold-start > 250ms.
test_plan: Chaos test: orchestrate correlated multi-tenant short bursts (30s-2m) in staging to validate new debounce settings and burst-index behavior.
Load test: run a 2-hour ramp with periodic 1-minute spikes at 3x baseline to ensure adaptive smoothing triggers scale-up without oscillation.
Warm-pool validation: exercise cohort retention logic by replaying recorded production burst sequences in an isolated env and assert warm instances >= 20% provisioned during bursts.
Automation: add regression tests to CI that assert no cold-start > 400ms were introduced by tuning changes.

comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial write-up completed after reviewing 1h of raw KEDA metric traces and HPA events. Short-term mitigations applied one hour post-incident. Creating ticket to track long-term engineering work.

2026-03-11 - Marco Li: Verified that lowering debounce reduced TTR in Canary. Observed one instance of overreaction to a synthetic microburst; adding upper-bound rate limiting on scale-ups in next patch.
2026-03-12 - Elena Gomez: Warm-pool eviction thresholds updated in staging and cohorting prototype validated with replayed traces. Will coordinate with Performance team for longer-run tests.
2026-03-13 - Priya Nair: Adaptive smoothing RFC drafted and posted to engineering docs. Requesting review from runtime and infra teams before scheduling implementation.
risks: Reducing debounce windows may increase false-positive scale-ups under noisy telemetry; mitigated by upper-bound rate limiting and burst-index validation.
More aggressive warm retention increases cost; cohorting logic must balance latency improvements against reserved capacity spend.
Changes to smoothing logic could interact with other autoscalers (HPA vs custom controllers) and need coordinated rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Staging chaos tests demonstrating no latency regression and no more than 10% false-positive scale-ups compared to baseline.
Production dashboards show scale-decision-latency median improvement of >= 30% for 1m spike events after rollout.
Runbook updated and SRE team trained on new escalation steps; on-call quiz completed by 2026-03-20.
notes: Follow-ups should be tracked as separate engineering tickets for each action item; this ticket will remain as the coordinator until all acceptance criteria met.
